name: agent-builder-agents-md-hygiene
body:
Law (prose; assessed by review): `AGENTS.md` hygiene is part of the `agent-builder`'s universal agent-management responsibility.
(1) NOTHING ABOUT THE FLOW: `AGENTS.md` must carry NOTHING about the canonical change-set flow — not a duplicate, not a summary, and not even a reference or pointer to the `codebase-navigator` prompt. The flow is owned SOLELY and IMMUTABLY by the distributed `codebase-navigator` prompt (`opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `requirements.requirement.navigator-staged-flow`). The agent-builder AUDITS `AGENTS.md` and REMOVES any flow content it finds; it never adds a reference/pointer to the navigator and never restates the flow itself. The agent-builder does NOT edit `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`.
(2) NON-DESTRUCTIVE MERGE: when `AGENTS.md` exists, the agent-builder may remove prose ONLY where it is change-set flow content or contradicts the distributed-agent rules; every repo-specific section (build gates, test tiers, pipeline, release steps, and all other repo-specific content) is preserved.
(3) ONLY WHEN PRESENT: `AGENTS.md` is optional per project; the agent-builder edits one only when it exists and never manufactures an `AGENTS.md`.
(4) MAIN-WRITE ACCOUNTING: the repo-root `AGENTS.md` is a MAIN-checkout write path of the agent-builder (carve-out 1 of `global.constraint.worktree-isolation`). Across the two carve-outs there are now FOUR main-write paths — `.opencode/agents/**`, the `opencode.json` agent→model map, `AGENTS.md`, and the release-agent's artefact set — with carve-out 1 covering three of them; the carve-out COUNT stays TWO. The `AGENTS.md` write rides the SAME carve-out, committed on main; `git push`/`git tag` remain human-approved acts.
(5) UNIVERSALITY: the law binds EVERY apg project. In the apg repo the local `build-implementer` also touches `AGENTS.md`; that is a repo-specific arrangement, not part of this universal rule.
